chapter: Union career, Masons, mentoring and the Clef Club
title: Howard and Collette's long friendship
summary: Howard praises Collette, whom he has known since boyhood, and tells how Collette's father introduced himself.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You're a beautiful man. He is. He is. I've known him so long, you'd be surprised how long I've known him.
Well, you told me the other day, you've known him since he was just a little child.
I did, as just a little tot, a little youngster, just running up and down the streets.
You wasn't in trouble. You never got in trouble, that's the thing about it.
He said you were a very good influence on him.

Yeah. He never got in trouble. A lot of the guys got in trouble. [make adjustment] I say a lot of fellows got in trouble, but not Buddy. Buddy's been a very, very, very excellent man to know, and I love him dearly, I really do. I certainly do.
Well, he describes you that very same way, as a very beautiful man that he loves very much.

And you know, his father -- oh, I want to tell you about his father. His father comes up the street the other day, lives down the street from me here, and he came here and was talking to me, and he said, "Do you know Buddy Collette?" I said, "What the hell are you talking about? Do I know him? He's one of the best men that I ever did know." And I told him that. And he said, "I'm his father." And I like to fell out. I didn't know his father. Didn't know him. Makes me feel kind of sad.
